items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Henry played bass horn with us.

ctx.x: See, like the Caledonian them on a band.

You know, like Howard would get a band up, you know, for the same thing. That's what he used to do. Black Benny would play. It wasn't Black Benny, it was Henry Martin on bass drums. I see. I see. I see. I see. I see. I see.
I see. I see. I see.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Henry Martin was the first one I seen do it.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. But, uh, we got tape after tape on dad. Yeah. Because I knew he was about to go and he needed a little comfort, you know. Yeah. And the friendship. He liked to see punch, you know. Uh-huh. All that. You mentioned a while back something about a guitar solo, how you'd come down for that?

Yeah. How the drummer would come down. He'd hit on, he'd play on the rim, crush roll on the rims. That's the way I did most of the drummers, Henry Martin, you know. Henry Zeno, most of us, that's the way we done. Play on the rim, see. Crush roll on the rims. It's something nice. Oh. With that beat off the cymbal, you see, on your bass drum. Just like you play your bass drum now, see.
And you took the cymbal out?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: my famous drummer, Henry Martin, at that time... I played in his drummer's place, in Henry Martin's place.

ctx.x: Bebe Ridgely's Tuxedo Band. I used to follow the parades, the street parades, and my famous drummer, Henry Martin, at that time.
